turns.query: Across three still pictures my scalloped larch grafting wedge acquires a different outline. How would I rebuild the reference from the beginning so later photos agree?
turns.answer:
To ensure your "scalloped larch grafting wedge" has a consistent outline across all your photos, you need to rebuild your product reference sheet from the beginning. Here's how, based on Lesson 02 of the AI Product Photoshoot & Ads course:

1.  **Take New Photos:** Capture 5-7 clear photos of your scalloped larch grafting wedge from different angles. Make sure to use daylight and turn off your phone's flash to get accurate details.
2.  **Start a New Project in Google Flow:** Go to Google Flow, select "New project," then "Image," and choose "Nano Banana Pro."
3.  **Upload Photos and Generate Product Sheet:** Upload all the new photos you took as references. Then, run the Product Sheet template.
4.  **Review and Regenerate:** Carefully check the generated product sheet. If the wedge's outline isn't consistent or looks different, regenerate the sheet until you get one that accurately represents your product from all angles.
5.  **Save the Best Sheet:** Once you have a good product sheet where the wedge's outline is consistent, save it. This will be your primary reference for all future product shots in the course.

By creating a strong, consistent product sheet, all subsequent photos generated using this reference will maintain the correct outline of your scalloped larch grafting wedge.

turns.query: I changed only the hue of my cork pot-lifter band, yet its rim moved. Explain the course correction and what should stay invariant.
turns.answer:
When you change only the color (hue) of your product, but its shape or other details change unexpectedly, it means the AI model didn't correctly understand your instruction to keep everything else the same.

The course correction for this is to explicitly tell the AI to preserve the original shape and details. You should use a prompt similar to: "Only change the colour... keep everything else exactly the same." and "Preserve the same shape and details as the reference sheet."

What should stay invariant (unchanged) is the product's:
*   **Shape**
*   **Details**
*   **Text and logo** (if any),

This ensures that only the color is modified, and the product's core identity remains consistent.

turns.query: I have a plain photo of a ribbed hazel cutting-guide puck and another where ribbon hides its edge. Compare their usefulness, choose the first reference, and explain one later use for the ribbon composition.
turns.answer:
Let's compare the two photos for creating AI product images:

**Comparison of Usefulness:**

*   **Plain photo of a ribbed hazel cutting-guide puck:** This photo is more useful as a primary reference. It clearly shows the entire product, including its shape, texture (ribbed), and details. For AI generation, having a complete and unobstructed view of the product is crucial for creating accurate product sheets and consistent images.
*   **Photo where ribbon hides its edge:** This photo is less useful as a primary reference because the ribbon obscures part of the product. When creating a product sheet or generating images, the AI needs to "see" the entire product to understand its form. If parts are hidden, the AI might generate incomplete or inaccurate representations.

**Decision:**

I recommend choosing the **plain photo of a ribbed hazel cutting-guide puck** as the first reference.

**Later Use for the Ribbon Composition:**

The photo with the ribbon hiding the edge could be useful later for creating a **festive or gift-themed product shot**. For example, in Lesson 04, the course covers creating festive shoots like wedding gifts. You could use the idea of the ribbon to inspire a prompt where the cutting-guide puck is presented as a gift, perhaps partially wrapped or with decorative ribbon around it, similar to the example in which mentions "gold ribbon" for a wedding gift scene. This would add a decorative element to your product photography without being the primary reference for the product itself.

सफेद फोटो (White Studio Photo) और सजावट वाले कमरे की फोटो (Lifestyle Photo) में मुख्य अंतर यह है:

**सफेद फोटो (White Studio Photo):**
*   इसमें आपका प्रोडक्ट "आसमानी ऊन की बीज बाँधने की पट्टी" एक सादे सफेद बैकग्राउंड पर होता है।
*   फोकस पूरी तरह से प्रोडक्ट पर होता है, ताकि उसकी डिटेल्स, रंग और बनावट साफ दिख सके।
*   यह आमतौर पर ई-कॉमर्स वेबसाइट्स या कैटलॉग के लिए इस्तेमाल होती है, जहाँ प्रोडक्ट को बिना किसी डिस्ट्रेक्शन के दिखाना होता है।

**सजावट वाले कमरे की फोटो (Lifestyle Photo):**
*   इसमें आपका प्रोडक्ट "आसमानी ऊन की बीज बाँधने की पट्टी" एक वास्तविक सेटिंग, जैसे कि सजावट वाले कमरे में दिखाया जाता है।
*   यह फोटो दिखाती है कि प्रोडक्ट असल जिंदगी में कैसा दिखेगा या कैसे इस्तेमाल होगा।
*   यह ग्राहकों को प्रोडक्ट के साथ एक भावनात्मक जुड़ाव महसूस कराने में मदद करती है और उन्हें यह कल्पना करने में मदद करती है कि वे इसे कैसे इस्तेमाल कर सकते हैं।
*   इस तरह की फोटो में प्रोडक्ट के साथ 2-3 और चीजें हो सकती हैं, लेकिन प्रोडक्ट हमेशा आगे और सजावट पीछे होनी चाहिए, जैसा कि में बताया गया है।

संक्षेप में, सफेद फोटो प्रोडक्ट की स्पष्टता पर जोर देती है, जबकि सजावट वाले कमरे की फोटो प्रोडक्ट के उपयोग और अनुभव को दर्शाती है।
